$comment: Tab 2 (WI-005 §3, E2): the seven Class A KSI blocks in playbook order and the Vulnerability detection block. Question ids are the intake numbers; texts are spec §3 verbatim. The KSI name and FedRAMP's statement come from the vendored rules, never from this file. howOften: 'required' = the question itself asks it (no separate line); 'optional' = a separate optional line that never affects the status; 'none' = no line. Changing a line here is a text change, not a code change.

labels.howOftenHelp: FedRAMP expects ongoing activities to run on a known, documented cycle.
labels.needHelp: I don't know, I need help from Ignyte with this one

questions.text: How do you check that security training works for all staff, high-risk roles, engineering staff, and incident response or recovery staff, and how often?

ksis.why: FedRAMP asks whether your training actually works, not just whether people took it, for all staff, high-risk roles, engineers, and incident response or recovery staff.

questions.text: How are production changes logged, who monitors those logs, and how often?

ksis.why: FedRAMP asks that changes to your service are both logged and monitored, including changes made outside your normal deployment process.

questions.text: How do you restrict inbound and outbound traffic, and how often do you review those rules? For example, firewalls, security groups, private subnets, allow-lists.

ksis.why: FedRAMP asks that you limit both incoming and outgoing traffic, and keep checking those limits over time.

questions.text: Which parts of creating, changing and removing accounts, roles and groups are automated, and which are still manual?

ksis.why: FedRAMP asks that accounts, roles and groups, and what they can access, are managed through automation rather than by hand.

questions.text: How do administrators and users sign in? Is MFA phishing-resistant (for example FIDO2 keys, passkeys, PIV)?
Where are passwords still used, and why?

ksis.why: FedRAMP expects passwordless sign-in where it's feasible; where passwords remain, it expects strong passwords with phishing-resistant MFA, so we need to know where they are.

questions.text: How do you review whether your incident response procedures work, how often, and what changed after the last review?

ksis.why: FedRAMP asks that you keep checking whether your incident response procedures actually work, not only that a plan exists.

questions.text: How is information protected from unwanted access or modification, at rest and in transit, and which crypto modules are used?

ksis.why: FedRAMP asks that information is protected from unwanted access or changes. Your consultant checks the encryption modules you list.

readiness.title: Vulnerability detection
readiness.note: Not one of the seven Class A KSIs. FedRAMP requires vulnerability detection at Class A; fixing timeframes are recommended, not required.

questions.text: How do you find vulnerabilities, using which methods, and how often?
questions.why: FedRAMP requires you to keep finding vulnerabilities, using methods that fit your service, such as scanning, testing, threat intelligence and disclosure reports.

questions.text: How are findings fixed, and within what timeframes?
questions.why: This helps us plan how quickly findings get fixed. FedRAMP recommends fix timeframes at Class A but doesn't require them.
